key_provisions_or_claims: Hip, knee and shoulder replacements are reclassified from class IIb to class III medical devices.
Defines a joint replacement as an implantable component; ancillary components excluded.
Transitional periods require complementary design examination by 2009 and 2010.
Member States must transpose by 1 March 2007 and apply from 1 September 2007.
Notified bodies must examine design dossiers and clinical data.
annotation.summary_en: Commission Directive 2005/50/EC reclassifies hip, knee and shoulder joint replacements from class IIb to class III under the Medical Devices Directive 93/42/EEC, requiring stricter notified-body design examination, with transitional arrangements and transposition deadlines. It concerns passive implants, not AI or robotics.
